answer: Rotation-Keyed Task Assignment works by assigning each new agent a task slot derived from a verifiable random beacon and the agent's key, so attackers cannot predict which slot they get. A violet token marks each valid slot; only the holder can claim it, and claiming requires solving a slot-specific puzzle. Because assignment depends on beacon output revealed after registration, mass-registering identities yields no advantage. Attacker cost scales with real compute per identity, reaching a zenith only through wasted parallel work. Each orchard of slots also expires, forcing repeated payment.
